President Trump has systematically broken virtually every promise made on the
campaign trail to court health-focused voters.

His most recent walk-backs on pesticide reform are a cruel insult to the idea
of “making America healthy again.” Among other controversies, he issued an
executive order to boost[ the production of
glyphosate](https://www.iarc.who.int/featured-news/media-centre-iarc-news-
glyphosate/), a toxic pesticide [linked to
cancer](https://www.iarc.who.int/featured-news/media-centre-iarc-news-
glyphosate/). And he’s
[repeatedly](https://www.foodandwaterwatch.org/2025/12/02/trump-admin-sides-
with-bayer-in-supreme-court-bid-to-block-pesticide-lawsuits/)
[sided](https://civileats.com/2026/03/03/trump-administration-affirms-support-
for-bayer-in-glyphosate-case/) with Bayer in a Supreme Court case that will
determine legal immunity from health-related lawsuits for pesticide
manufacturers.

Voters of both parties are hungry for a new path forward.

America’s food and agriculture industries have never been as consolidated as
they are now. This dominance means that just a few corporations, driven by
profit margins and shareholder dividends, are calling all the shots about what
makes its way onto our plates. And it’s making us sick.

Take pesticides. America is a nation smothered in toxic chemicals. Some [81
percent of U.S. residents have glyphosate in their
urine](https://www.cdc.gov/biomonitoring/featured-work/diet-is-a-factor-in-
contact-with-glyphosate.html), and [pesticides increasingly contain
PFAS](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39046250/) “forever chemicals,” which
are [in nearly everyone’s
blood](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4483690/).

Several of the products farmers and gardeners use today are known or suspected
to cause cancer, birth defects, Parksinsons’ disease, and more. Many have been
banned or restricted in other countries. In some rural communities,[just
living near pesticide-treated fields](https://inthesetimes.com/article/study-
agriculture-pesticides-cancer-risk-farm-towns) has been linked to cancer risk
on par with smoking.

The vast majority of pesticides are used on crops grown for ethanol and
factory farm animal feed. This meat from factory farms is not the “real food”
Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr.’s Super Bowl ad wants you to believe.

Factory-farmed animals are raised in cruel conditions, spending their lives on
top of each other, covered in their own waste. Animals raised in these
conditions are fed pesticide-ridden feed and antibiotics. And like any
factory, these operations discharge dangerous pollution, driving a[ cancer-
linked drinking water crisis in several
states](https://newrepublic.com/article/201118/corn-cancer-iowa-deadly-water-
crisis).

It’s no surprise that[ more than 70 percent of American
adults](https://www.pew.org/en/research-and-
analysis/articles/2026/02/26/americans-are-concerned-about-harmful-chemicals-
in-food-water-and-everyday-products) are concerned about toxic chemical
exposure in their food and drinking water. But to truly make America healthy
again, we need to break up Big Ag once and for all.

President Trump once criticized America’s food monopolies. In[ November
2024](https://x.com/realDonaldTrump/status/1857170020427595797?lang=en), he
called out the “industrial food complex” and pledged “that everybody will be
protected from harmful chemicals, pollutants, pesticides… and food additives
that have contributed to [an] overwhelming health crisis.”

But a year into his second term, Trump and Kennedy Jr. have done more to
_solidify_ those monopolies than to challenge them.

Corporate profits are at the heart of America’s pesticide and factory farm
crises. A select few companies dominate the agrichemical sector, locking
farmers into a treadmill of dependence on toxic pesticides and the seeds bred
to withstand them.

Today, [just two companies own 90 percent of the genetic traits of domestic
corn, soybeans, and cotton](https://farmaction.us/concentrationdata/). One of
them, Bayer, is the German mega-corporation behind Roundup — America’s most
used pesticide. The World Health Organization classifies Roundup’s active
ingredient, glyphosate, as likely carcinogenic. [Tens of thousands of
Americans](https://www.reuters.com/business/healthcare-pharmaceuticals/bayer-
make-105-bln-push-settle-roundup-cases-bloomberg-reports-2026-02-17/)have
pending or settled cancer lawsuits against the corporation.

Meanwhile, just four companies control [81 percent of the beef market, 65
percent of the pork
market](https://www.ams.usda.gov/sites/default/files/media/PackersandStockyards2021_2022ReporttoCongress.pdf),
and 55 percent of the poultry market.

The Trump administration’s [unscientific dietary
guidelines](https://www.foodandwaterwatch.org/2026/01/16/trump-dietary-
guidelines-meat-big-ag/) are a gift to these corporations. By promoting animal
protein consumption at rates far above the recommendation of most doctors,
Trump is pushing for more factory farming — and thus more power for the
monopolies. And Americans’ health will pay the price.

Trump has the power to restrict pesticides and transition meat production out
of the factory farm model. Instead he’s doubling down, backing pesticide
manufacturers’[ quest to evade
culpability](https://www.foodandwaterwatch.org/2025/08/08/inside-bayers-
cancer-gag-act-push/) for terrible health impacts.

Trump’s disingenuous pledges to “make America healthy again” are nothing but
lies, designed to distract from his real goal of bolstering Big Ag, not taking
it on.
